envelope.author: nico
envelope.reason: corrected-shards ended with two branches: the integration line held every approved unit but none of the 53 records written on the build branch, so neither alone was the release and the operator had to ask which branch held the work
envelope.cause: operator: there should be one branch with all our work integrated

payload.gloss: the role that makes approved work whole: it takes each unit whose assay verdict is achieved, combines it with the work already approved on the plan's one line, and confirms the whole still holds by running the project's full check once, so no implementer has to. That line is where the plan's whole work lives: every approved unit together with every design, plan and note record written while the plan ran, so releasing it loses nothing and no other branch holds anything it lacks. A failure names the unit it came from and returns to that unit's implementer by way of the architect. It decides nothing about the design and repairs nothing itself; releasing the finished whole is the operator's sign-off.
